harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as an HTTP load-balancing entry point on its management address 10.100.3.10:80 using the os-haproxy plugin, round-robin balancing across HTTP backends on node2 (10.100.3.11:8080) and node3 (10.100.3.12:8080), each running a Python http.server that identifies itself. Verified node4 receives responses from both backends through this single entry point. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time native reboot protocol on all four nodes (node2, node3, node4, node1) with captured pre/post boot-identity proof and post-restart service recovery, finishing with a final check from node4 confirming continued balanced responses through node1's port 80 after every restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1 is OPNsense/FreeBSD with a single LAN interface (vtnet0, 10.100.3.10/24) shared with node2 (AlmaLinux, 10.100.3.11), node3 (AlmaLinux, 10.100.3.12), node4 (AlmaLinux, 10.100.3.13)
Deployed a systemd-managed Python http.server on node2 and node3 bound to 0.0.0.0:8080, each serving a static page identifying the host
Opened TCP/8080 in firewalld on node2 and node3 (previously blocked, causing connection-refused from node1)
Installed the os-haproxy plugin on node1 via pkg

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 (with a backup copy) via a Python ElementTree script to add two HAProxy servers (node2:8080, node3:8080), one HTTP backend with algorithm=roundrobin linking both servers, and one HTTP frontend bound to 10.100.3.10:80 with defaultBackend set; fixed a missing required connectionBehaviour field that had broken the generated haproxy.conf
Discovered and disabled OPNsense's lighttpd HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect on port 80 (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect=1), which was occupying the wildcard :80 listener and blocking HAProxy's explicit bind
Regenerated the HAProxy template (configctl template reload), validated syntax (haproxy -c), deployed, and started the haproxy service, confirming it listens on 10.100.3.10:80
Verified round-robin load balancing locally from node1 and end-to-end from node4 (even 5/5 and 4/4 splits across repeated requests)
Captured a healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data checks) on all 4 nodes

Rebooted node2, node3, node4, and node1 one at a time using each OS's native reboot command, confirming SSH/exec disconnect-then-reconnect and a changed boot identity (boot_id or kern.boottime) for each

After each restart, confirmed recovery: node2/node3 simplehttp and firewalld active with correct HTTP responses; node4 still able to reach the LB entry point; node1's haproxy auto-started via haproxy_enable=YES and resumed listening on 10.100.3.10:80
Performed a final end-to-end verification from node4 after node1's restart, confirming balanced responses from both node2 and node3 through the single port-80 entry point

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 serve identifying HTTP content on port 8080 on the shared private network
evidence.summary: systemd services started on node2/node3; node1 curl to 10.100.3.11:8080 and 10.100.3.12:8080 returns 'Hello from node2' / 'Hello from node3' respectively

evidence.requirement: node1 presents a single entry point on TCP port 80 of its management address that spreads requests across node2 and node3
evidence.summary: haproxy listening on 10.100.3.10:80 (sockstat); repeated curl to 10.100.3.10:80 from node1 alternates 'Hello from node2'/'Hello from node3' in round-robin order

evidence.requirement: node4 receives answers from each backend through node1's entry point
evidence.summary: node4 curling http://10.100.3.10/ ten times yields a 5/5 split between 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3'

evidence.requirement: healthy baseline captured before any restarts
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot identity (kern.boottime for node1, boot_id for node2/3/4) plus service-active and HTTP-response checks on each node

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled and acknowledged; subsequent exec times out (disconnect); boot_id changes from 31b01b46... to cabe7f2d...; simplehttp/firewalld active and HTTP response restored post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled; exec times out during reboot; boot_id changes from e31962a9... to f6fa136b...; simplehttp/firewalld active and HTTP response restored post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled; exec times out during reboot; boot_id changes from d527ba47... to c73264ab...; post-reboot node4 still receives balanced 4/4 responses through node1's LB, proving its own network/service function recovered

evidence.requirement: node1 (OPNsense) restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery of LB service and cluster function
evidence.summary: shutdown -r scheduled and acknowledged; subsequent exec (SSH) times out during reboot; kern.boottime changes from 16:24:15 to 16:30:49; haproxy auto-restarted and listening on 10.100.3.10:80 post-reboot; final node4 check shows continued 4/4 balanced responses through the recovered entry point
